events.title: AngularJS 0.9.0 open-sourced
events.summary: Miško Hevery open-sourced AngularJS 0.9.0 on October 20, 2010 — two-way data binding and MVC for single-page web apps.
events.about: AngularJS let HTML drive the UI with directives and `ng-model` two-way binding — no manual DOM updates for forms and lists. It powered early Google products and enterprise SPAs before React and Vue. Developers learned `$scope`, dependency injection, and the digest cycle on countless internal dashboards.

narrative.whyChosen: AngularJS popularized declarative SPAs and two-way binding in mainstream web development.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced every later frontend framework's component and data-binding models.
narrative.problemSolved: jQuery spaghetti could not scale; teams needed structure for complex client-side applications.

events.title: NuGet released
events.summary: Microsoft released NuGet 1.0 on October 5, 2010 — a package manager for .NET libraries, originally named NuPack.
events.about: NuGet brought `Install-Package Newtonsoft.Json` to Visual Studio and `dotnet add package` to the CLI — centralizing .NET dependencies the way npm did for Node. The nuget.org gallery hosts millions of packages; SDK-style projects and CI pipelines assume NuGet restore. It completed the .NET ecosystem's shift from copying DLLs into `lib/` folders.

narrative.whyChosen: NuGet standardized dependency management for the .NET platform.
narrative.whyImportant: It enabled reusable open-source libraries and reproducible builds across the Microsoft stack.
narrative.problemSolved: .NET teams manually vendored binaries with no shared registry or version resolution.

events.title: Shopware Community Edition released
events.summary: Shopware released its free Community Edition in autumn 2010 — open-sourcing the core e-commerce platform on the same technical base as paid editions.
events.about: The Community Edition let developers download and extend Shopware without licensing fees — download records broke company targets overnight. It paved the way for the full AGPL open-source release in Shopware 4 two years later.

narrative.whyChosen: Shopware's Community Edition brought enterprise e-commerce features to the open-source crowd.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved a commercial vendor could grow through community-driven development.
narrative.problemSolved: European developers lacked a free, full-featured alternative to paid cart software.
